reasons: Fallback images and error paths exist for missing WebGL and reduced motion.
Shader failures are only logged, not shown or reported.
Complex and hard to review; no tests seen.

terms.meaning: a browser technology that lets code draw using the computer's graphics card
a small program that runs on the graphics card to decide each pixel's colour
an image loaded onto the graphics card for shaders to read
a value passed from the page to a shader that stays the same across one drawing pass
a small grid of values that records where the pointer has been and fades over time

sections.name: File setup, Annotate (part 1)
sections.title: Shader text and shared setup
sections.what: Holds the graphics program text: a simple vertex program and the start of the fragment program, with its inputs and sampling helpers.
sections.why: Shader code runs on the graphics card, so it is stored here as text.
sections.watch_out: Shader syntax errors show only in the console at runtime.

sections.name: File setup, Annotate (part 2)
sections.title: Distortion field lookup and block layout
sections.what: Looks up the distortion field and chooses a block shape for each region of the picture.
sections.why: Mixed block shapes keep the broken look irregular rather than circular.
sections.watch_out: Fixed sizes such as 96 and 48 set the look, so changing them changes every image.

sections.name: File setup, Annotate: if
sections.title: Block shifts, slivers, and scanlines
sections.what: Decides which blocks are shifted or striped, which small slivers appear, and how horizontal scanlines move. Then mixes colour, noise, and monochrome.
sections.why: Adds the film-like texture of the effect.
sections.watch_out: The strength value scales every shift, so high values can hide the picture.

sections.name: PixelImageProps
sections.title: Options a caller can pass
sections.what: Lists the inputs: source or placeholder, alt text, mode, focus point, monochrome, annotation style, revealed flag, strength, class name, and priority.
sections.why: Documents the public inputs for anyone using the component.
sections.watch_out: Mode must be distort or reveal, and other values silently change behaviour.

sections.name: Pointer
sections.title: Pointer state
sections.what: Stores the pointer's position, speed, whether it is over the image, and whether a touch is holding it.

sections.name: PixelImage (part 1)
sections.title: Component start and revealed state
sections.what: Reads the options, sets up references to the canvas and overlay labels, keeps the fallback image and natural size, and restarts the loop when the revealed flag changes.
sections.why: The revealed flag can change from outside, such as a tap on touch screens.

sections.name: PixelImage (part 2)
sections.title: Placeholder and fallback setup
sections.what: Creates a placeholder picture when no file is given, waiting for fonts. Uses it, or the plain fallback image, when WebGL is unavailable or reduced motion is set. Compiles and links the shaders.
sections.why: The page still works on devices without WebGL or with reduced motion.
sections.watch_out: If shader compilation fails, the function returns without a message to the user and the canvas stays blank.

sections.name: PixelImage (part 3)
sections.title: Buffers, inputs, and textures
sections.what: Creates the vertex buffer, sets the shader inputs, creates two textures, and sets up the distortion field grid.
sections.why: The field is kept as a small grid so it is cheap to update.
sections.watch_out: The field is reset when the grid height changes.

sections.name: PixelImage (part 4)
sections.title: Sizing and covering the frame
sections.what: Tracks the pointer, box, and timing. Works out how the image fills its frame with the focus point, and resizes the canvas at device resolution.
sections.why: Cover means the image fills the box without stretching.
sections.watch_out: Focus values should stay between 0 and 1.

sections.name: PixelImage (part 5)
sections.title: Updating the distortion field
sections.what: Each frame, fades the field and adds to it where the pointer or touch hold is. Reports whether anything is still changing.
sections.why: The field fades so the image heals after the pointer leaves.
sections.watch_out: Every grid cell is checked each frame, so grid size affects cost.

sections.name: PixelImage (part 6)
sections.title: Tracking box and coordinates
sections.what: Moves the crosshair, the live coordinate readout, the tracking box, and its size label when annotations are on.
sections.why: Gives project images a technical, measured look.
sections.watch_out: Skipped entirely when annotations are set to none.

sections.name: PixelImage (part 7)
sections.title: Drawing a frame and the loop
sections.what: Sends the field and settings to the graphics card and draws one frame. Runs the animation loop only while something changes, and provides a wake function to restart it.
sections.watch_out: The loop stops off screen; the wake function is what restarts it.

sections.name: PixelImage (part 8)
sections.title: Pointer and visibility events
sections.what: Turns pointer movement into field updates, clears the pointer on leave, toggles the hold on touch taps, and watches size and visibility.
sections.why: Touch devices cannot hover, so a tap toggles the effect.
sections.watch_out: Touch movement is ignored; only taps affect touch.

sections.name: PixelImage (part 9)
sections.title: Loading the image into a texture
sections.what: Loads the image or placeholder asynchronously into a texture, then starts the loop and marks the component ready.
sections.why: Loading in the background keeps the page from waiting.
sections.watch_out: A failed image load returns early, leaving the fallback visible.

sections.name: PixelImage (part 10)
sections.title: Rendered markup and annotations
sections.what: Renders the wrapper, the fallback image, the canvas, and the overlay with labels, corner ticks, the tracking box, and the crosshair.
sections.why: The fallback image appears before the canvas is ready.
sections.watch_out: The fallback uses the same focus point as the canvas, so framing matches.

summary: The site's shared image effect. A picture breaks into blocks and fragments, and the pointer rebuilds it locally. It is drawn with WebGL on the graphics card.
purpose: Used for the hero portrait and project images to give them a consistent, technical look.
why: A single shared component keeps the effect the same everywhere.
how: Loads the image or a generated placeholder into a texture. Each frame, the pointer adds to a low-resolution distortion field, which decays over time. A fragment program turns the field into blocks, shifts, and noise. Optional annotations show coordinates and a tracking box.
inputs: An image path or a placeholder description, alt text, mode (distort or reveal), focus point, monochrome amount, annotation style, revealed flag, strength, and priority.
outputs: A canvas that shows the effect, with a plain image shown first as a fallback. When annotations are on, live coordinates and boxes appear over the image.
risks: The effect runs many calculations each frame, so it can be slow on weak devices. Shader errors only write warnings to the console and leave the canvas blank.
debug: If the image stays as a plain fallback, check the browser for WebGL support and shader warnings in the console. If the image is blank, check the texture load and the asset path. If the animation keeps running, check the wake and visibility logic. If the effect looks wrong after a size change, check the field size reset.
